brief:
A commander in the Radeet force, a resistance group operating in Gaza, said the organization has documented senior collaborators from what he characterized as "client gangs" purchasing apartments and residential properties in Arab countries outside the strip, Shehab Wire reported. The commander did not specify which countries were involved or provide figures on the number of properties acquired.

The statement reflects ongoing tensions between Palestinian armed groups and individuals accused of collaborating with Israeli forces. The commander's disclosure suggests that Radeet has established some form of monitoring capability to track financial transactions and asset purchases by alleged collaborators beyond Gaza's borders, though he offered no details about the methods or extent of such surveillance.
